axes.model_access: Academic retrieval system + LLM extraction pipeline: a self-built paper index (Semantic Scholar-family academic libraries as one underlying layer, official narrative) + multiple LLMs doing extraction/synthesis (official narrative, not inventoried item by item).
axes.runtime: Web (elicit.com) as the main entry; literature retrieval and extraction generation both happen on the vendor's cloud; no officially stated local form seen.
axes.local_files: Projects/literature libraries stored on the account-side cloud; exports (CSV/review documents) count as local. No officially stated local data surface seen.
axes.background: Retrieval is instant; systematic-review style tasks (multi-round screening/extraction tables) are a task line; no "keep-running-after-shutdown" concept.
axes.tools: **Literature retrieval + structured extraction is the main axis**: searching papers by research question, screening (inclusion/exclusion criteria surface), extraction tables (sample/method/conclusion columns), review synthesis (with citations); a "find similar papers" line (official product surface).
axes.context: Literature work organized by project; cross-session memory not verified to an official statement.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system (D9: pricing not collected); free-tier retrieval/extraction quota limits not verified item by item; the training-use switch not verified item by item.
axes.fit: Fits: systematic reviews/literature surveys (medicine/social sciences/ML and other English literature pools), researchers who want "extraction tables" rather than "reading abstracts". Does not fit: Chinese-literature-first (the academic libraries are English-leaning), non-academic retrieval, wanting full-text access (it anchors abstracts and available full-text snippets).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creation products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Accuracy of numeric fields in extraction tables** (sampling against the originals)
- **The set difference between retrieval recall and a manual PubMed search**
- **The free-tier quota boundary** (retrieval/extraction counts)
unknowns:
- The underlying academic-library list and coverage (official narrative says Semantic Scholar-family, not verified item by item)
- The LLM list currently in use (not inventoried item by item)
- ToS details (CF 403 blocked direct fetch)
- The training-use switch (not verified item by item)
related: Source-anchoring contrast: Elicit finds sources then anchors, NotebookLM only anchors the sources you give it.
Also scientific-literature oriented: Consensus leads with "conclusion polarity" retrieval, Elicit leads with review extraction.
Chinese academic retrieval counterpart: Metaso has Chinese libraries/an academic tier, Elicit's English pool is deep.
